stories.title: Dolly Parton died after 'brief battle with cancer'
stories.summary: Country music star Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer", her publicist has said. In a statement to media outlets, her publicist Marcel Pariseau said: "After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones." The singer, 80, was best known for her genre-defining hits including 9 To 5, I Will Always Love You and Jolene. The statement continued: "Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand.

stories.title: How Dolly Parton changed young lives in Ireland
stories.summary: The family of Dolly Parton has asked those wishing to honour the late country music star to support one of the causes closest to her heart, her Imagination Library. Following Parton's death at the age of 80, her family asked that, in lieu of flowers, donations be made to the children's literacy programme she founded more than 30 years ago. Parton established the Imagination Library in her native Sevier County, Tennessee, in 1995, inspired by her father, Robert Lee Parton, who was unable to read or write. Speaking on The Late Late Show in 2022, Parton told Ryan Tubridy that her father's experience had stayed with her throughout her life.

stories.title: Harris indicates further budget measures on fuel poverty
stories.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris has said that diesel and petrol prices were in a very different place when the Government made the decision to gradually restore excise from 1 September. "You can see how quickly the global environment can change in four to six weeks. So we have to be humble, agile, and nimble enough to respond to things," he said. Mr Harris said the excise cuts were costing roughly around €100 million per month, which would be funded by running a smaller budget surplus. He also indicated that there would be further measures in the budget to combat fuel poverty.

stories.title: Caffeine in Costa cappuccino 3 times that of Starbucks
stories.summary: Coffee drinkers may be getting more or less caffeine in their drinks than they anticipated, with levels varying "wildly" between popular chains, a new study shows. The latest research from UK consumer champion Which? analyses the caffeine content in an array of drinks sold by chains Caffe Nero, Costa Coffee, Greggs, Pret A Manger and Starbucks. It found that a medium cappuccino from Costa contains 325 milligrams (mg) - almost three-and-a-half times as much as the same drink at Starbucks, at 89mg. The caffeine content in Costa's cappuccino is the equivalent of around four cans of Red Bull, Which? found.

stories.title: Israel threat on Gazan children's kites 'outrageous' - UN
stories.summary: The United Nations has condemned Israel's threat to expel people from areas where kites are launched from within Gaza, describing the comments by Israeli leaders as "unacceptable rhetoric". "On the threat of expulsion due to children's kite flying, I hope we can all agree that this is outrageous," UN rights office spokeswoman Ravina Shamdasani told reporters in Geneva. Israel has warned Hamas that it would step up operations in Gaza over what it claimed were launches of kites, drones and balloons towards Israel. Hamas has rejected the claims. Bassem Naim, a member of Hamas's political bureau, said in a statement that the kites were "launched from Gaza by children searching for their innocent childhood amid the rubble".

stories.title: Parrott enjoys winning debut as Betis snatch late victory
stories.summary: Troy Parrott made an impressive impact on his Real Betis debut to help his new side dig out a 1-0 La Liga win at Valencia on Tuesday night. The Republic of Ireland striker, who joined the Seville club from AZ Alkmaar last week, was summoned from the bench by boss Manuel Pellegrini in the 71st minute of a tight contest at the Mestalla. Parrott had a golden chance to break the deadlock almost immediately, beating the hosts' offside trap to race goalwards before dragging an angled effort just past the post. However in the 83rd minute, Betis did get the all-important breakthrough, and Parrott was heavily involved.

stories.title: McManus: Some county boards view hurling as a 'nuisance'
stories.summary: Former Antrim hurler Neil McManus believes that some county boards regard hurling as a "nuisance" and that counties that ignore the game should be penalised in terms of grants from Croke Park. At the elite level, the 2026 hurling championship was widely viewed as an unsatisfying affair, with an unusually high number of lop-sided games in the Munster championship, culminating in a drab All-Ireland final. While there had been humdrum hurling championships in the past, in 2026 an unflattering light was cast by a newly invigorated football championship, where both the playing rules and the competition format had contributed to one of the most exciting seasons in living memory. Some observers have contended that the commentariat are over-reacting to a single underwhelming campaign but McManus feels the sport has deeper structural issues that need addressing.

stories.title: Palmer stars as Alonso's Chelsea make perfect start
stories.summary: Xabi Alonso made a winning start to life as Chelsea manager in a chaotic 3-2 win over Fulham at Craven Cottage. It took only 31 seconds for Joao Pedro's goal to bring the visitors’ new era to life, but despite an attacking display that was scintillating at times, plenty still remained of the defensive frailties that have undermined this team in the recent past. Robert Sanchez’s hopeless attempt to keep out Josh King’s first-half equaliser was a reminder of areas of the pitch where Chelsea remain weak despite spending around £350million this summer. That outlay included a record £117m (€136m) lavished on Morgan Rogers. The England forward enjoyed an encouraging debut capped with a slotted finish to make it 2-1 before the break, then Cole Palmer, arguably Chelsea’s best player on the night, began the second half with a beautiful finish to make it three.

stories.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has named a 36-player training squad ahead of the upcoming WXV Global series, with seven uncapped players included in the group. Wing Beibhinn Parsons has been selected, despite picking up an injury ahead of Connacht's Interprovincial championship campaign. Former captain Edel McMahon, who has been training with Connacht this summer on her return from double knee surgery, is not involved in the Ireland squad. McMahon’s Exeter Chiefs team-mate Nancy McGillivray is also left out, despite featuring in three of Ireland’s five Guinness Women’s Six Nations games earlier this year.

stories.title: Seventeen countries, one van - a true story of hope and healing
stories.summary: We present an extract from One Year, the new memoir by Susan Bennett. Susan Bennett and her husband Chris are living normal, busy lives until their mid-thirties when a shock diagnosis of multiple sclerosis is delivered to both of them – in the same week, in the same hospital. This is one in a series of final straws that nudges them to follow their dream, simplify their lives, and take to the road for a year in their trusty camper van, Hans. One Year charts their journey around western Europe and Scandinavia. On a bright afternoon after 10 slow Scottish days, we arrived in Alnwick, with its castle, Titanic links and, most important of all, one of the best second-hand bookshops in the world. Turning a train station from the 1920s into a bookshop was a stroke of genius. Barter Books is long, tall and has gorgeous green tiles lining the walls, as well as real fire-places in little nooks where you can drink cups of tea. There's even a cute toy train on tracks above your head, swooshing along above great literary quotations. As I wandered happily among the shelves, the realisation that I now lived in a van was sinking in – I could not buy a book since it wouldn’t fit in our full cupboards. We need to buy less stuff. Things don’t make you happy... I had enjoyed my perch on this particular high horse when it involved things other than books, but now I struggled.

stories.title: Long-distance love stories: How these couples made it work
stories.summary: Long-distance isn't typically the first choice for those in committed relationships, but what length would you go to maintain a connection while separated by land and sea? Back in June, I sent a letter to Buenos Aires for my partner's 30th birthday. Although I sent it two weeks in advance, thinking it would make it on time, the package still hadn't arrived by mid-August. Obviously, a spiral ensued on my end at missing such a milestone birthday, particularly as he was such a big part of my 30th. It struck me that if we weren’t video-calling each other every day - not to mention sending a steady flow of memes and photo updates - that I would probably have lost some semblance of sanity at never getting a response or explanation.

stories.summary: Members of the Fórsa trade union employed at the Oberstown Children Detention Campus in Dublin are to escalate their industrial action in a dispute over resourcing and staffing levels. The industrial action is the fourth in a series of planned weekly work stoppages, which began earlier this month. Fórsa said there will be no derogations for social care work during the action and that the only derogation in place will be for campus catering.

stories.title: New financial services employment strategy launched
stories.summary: The Government has today launched a strategy to grow employment in the international financial services sector to 70,000 by 2030, with one in four of the jobs located outside of Dublin. The sector's 600 firms currently employ around 61,000 people across the country. The Ireland for Finance Strategy contains 31 actions designed to cut red tape, strengthen Ireland's competitiveness as an international financial services centre, and support innovation. The plan contains a major focus on technology and digital transformation, including AI, digital assets and tokenisation.

stories.title: Norway to crack down on use of smart glasses
stories.summary: Norwegian officials have said the country is planning to regulate the use of smart glasses and similar devices, and was considering a ban on features that enable facial recognition in public spaces. Smart glasses allow the wearer to shoot photos and videos, listen to music, take phone calls, translate signs in a foreign language, project text or maps into your field of view, or interact with an integrated AI assistant. "We can see that people's private lives and privacy are coming under pressure from new technology, and I therefore want to regulate smart glasses and similar devices more strictly than today," Digitalisation Minister Karianne Tung said in a statement. "This could, for example, mean banning features such as facial recognition of other people in public spaces," she said.

stories.title: Zelensky sees window for US mediation to end Ukraine war
stories.summary: Ukraine sees a window of opportunity for US mediation to end its war with Russia, its president has said, which runs from this December until the end of summer 2027. Volodymyr Zelensky has, together with US and European officials, drafted a page of suggestions which will be presented to Moscow to end the conflict which began when Russia invaded its neighbour four-and-a-half years ago. Mr Zelensky said a ceasefire and a previously discussed US proposal for a free economic zone in Ukraine's eastern Donbas area - to be administered by a third party - were among the ideas in the document. "It contains one of the ideas for a ceasefire - that is the main point. The second part concerns what the Americans proposed regarding a free economic zone," Mr Zelensky told reporters in a weekend briefing.

stories.title: Pollard returns as Boks makes changes for second Test
stories.summary: Rassie Erasmus has responded to Saturday's heavy defeat to New Zealand by making potentially four changes to his side ahead of this weekend’s second Test in Cape Town. Out-half Handre Pollard, wing Ethan Hooker and scrum-half Cobus Reinach all come into the starting XV following the 33-16 defeat to the All Blacks, while Siya Kolisi could also be among the starting team if he can prove his fitness. The regular captain missed Saturday’s loss on Johannesburg due to a hamstring injury, and will start at blindside flanker if cleared to play, with Erasmus confirming that Paul de Villiers will continue in the starting team if Kolisi doesn’t come through the week. The 17-point defeat was the heaviest the Springboks have had under Erasmus, and the World Cup-winning coach has responded by naming his side early ahead of Saturday’s second Test at DHL Stadium.

stories.title: Let's dance! RTÉ Radio 1 brings the Céilí Mór to Electric Picnic
stories.summary: The celebrated Clare ensemble will perform a selection of traditional favourites, accompanied by expert set dancers who will demonstrate some of Ireland's best-loved céilí dances and invite festivalgoers to join in the fun. In a unique meeting of tradition and innovation, the event will then see two-time World Champion turntablist Djackulate (AKA Jack Dempsey Mc Mahon) rework and sample recordings from the Kilfenora Céilí Band's rich musical archive into a brand-new live composition. The performance will culminate in a special collaboration as members of the Kilfenora Céilí Band join Djackulate on stage for a one-off musical fusion of traditional Irish music and contemporary turntablism. Djackulate, the stage name of Dublin-born and based Jack Dempsey Mc Mahon, is a multi-instrumentalist, turntablist, sample artist, uilleann piper and saxophone player. Internationally recognised for his innovative approach to sound, he has earned multiple world championship titles and is known for blending traditional and contemporary musical influences in unexpected ways.

stories.title: Underground Kerry hot spot wins Bar of the Year 2026
stories.summary: An underground bar in Killarney, Co. Kerry, has taken home the title of 'Bar of the Year' at the 2026 awards. Pig's Lane is a candle-lit haven known for its hand-crafted cocktails, vegan wines, locally sourced snacks and live music, not to mention a whiskey parlour packed with over 400 rare, quality bottles. Founded by Gemma Ring, owner of the O'Donoghue Ring Collection, a family-run Kerry hotel and hospitality group, the award-winning venue has become a popular destination since it opened in 2023. Built on the site of the original Pig’s Lane, a laneway dating back to the 1800s, the subterranean venue can be found within Killarney Towers Hotel on College Street.

stories.title: PSNI officer sacked over sexual relationship with victim
stories.summary: A police officer in Northern Ireland has been sacked for having a sexual relationship with a woman he met during an investigation, intimidating a former partner and attempting to falsify evidence. He is the seventh PSNI officer to be dismissed as a result of investigations into allegations of abuse of position for sexual purposes since 2020, and more than 60 cases have been reported since 2018 with each alleged victim classed as a "vulnerable" individual. A report by the Police Ombudsman for Northern Ireland published today has described the officer's behaviour as "a catalogue of corruption" which had the potential "to do serious damage to public trust and confidence in policing". He was also found to have failed to declare multiple conflicts of interest and asked a colleague to lie.

stories.title: Iran vows to resist sanctions, says US wants a deal
stories.summary: Iran has vowed to fight back against expanded US sanctions aimed at isolating its economy, expressing confidence that major trading partners would resist the pressure campaign and saying that Washington was keen to revive talks. Almost six months into a conflict the US has struggled to resolve, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled the measures on Monday but stopped short of the most punishing sanctions. While he said countries that continued trading with Iran risked being forced out of the dollar-based financial system, he declined to give a timeline or identify which may be targeted, saying he would give them time to comply with the new directive. Abbas Golroo, head of the foreign relations committee in the Iranian parliament, said Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir had delivered a message from the US to Iran on Monday.

stories.title: Feely already dreaming of scaling senior heights in 2027
stories.summary: While the achievements of this year are still very fresh in her mind, Roscommon's Aisling Feely is eagerly anticipating the prospect of playing senior championship football in 2027. Courtesy of their emphatic 2-12 to 0-06 triumph over Fermanagh in the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship decider at Croke Park on 2 August, the Rossies will be one of 12 counties to feature in the top-tier of the LGFA next summer. Even before taking part in the race for the Brendan Martin Cup, the primrose and blue will lock horns with newly-crowned All-Ireland senior winners Galway and Mayo in next year’s Connacht championship at the highest grade of ladies football. This will help to make it a three-team series out in the west once again, as it was when the previous season’s All-Ireland intermediate champions Leitrim made the brief step up to senior football in 2025, and Feely is excited about this new opportunity for Roscommon. "We saw Leitrim do it two years ago. We would have been always there or thereabouts with them. They knocked us out in the quarter-final that year by two points and they went on to win it. That gave us a bit of inspiration. If Leitrim can do it, why can’t we. We’re just as good. To get up to senior is absolutely massive," Feely acknowledged.
